q: Which Schedule of the Indian Constitution has a list of 22 languages recognised by the Constitution?
explanation: The 22 languages are in the Eighth Schedule (originally 14; Sindhi, Konkani, Manipuri, Nepali, Bodo, Dogri, Maithili and Santhali added later). The 9th Schedule protects land laws, the 10th is anti-defection, the 7th the legislative lists.

notes.text: - **Eighth Schedule = languages recognised by the Constitution** (Arts. **344(1) and 351**) – the "regional languages" / "official languages" schedule; **not** the Fourth, Sixth, Seventh or Ninth.
- **Number:** originally **14**, now **22** (not 18, 21 or 24).

q: While Hindi is the official language, English has been permitted for official use
explanation: The Official Languages Act 1963 (amended 1967) allows English to continue alongside Hindi for official purposes indefinitely.

notes.text: - Official language provisions = **Part XVII, Arts. 343–351**.

q: Which of the below mentioned schedules of the Constitution would undergo a change if a new State is created?
explanation: The First Schedule lists the names and territories of the States and UTs, so creating a new State amends it (the Fourth Schedule changes too, but it is not an option).

notes.text: - **New State created → First Schedule changes** (names and territories; the Fourth changes too when Rajya Sabha seats are re-allotted).

exam: APPSC Assistant Social, B.C. & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains
q: Regarding schedules of the Constitution, choose the wrong answer
options: Fourth Schedule - allocation of seats in the council of states
Fifth schedule - Provisions as to the Administration and control of schedule areas and schedule tribes
Eleventh Schedule - Powers, Authority and responsibilities of Municipalities
key_text: Eleventh Schedule - Powers, Authority and responsibilities of Municipalities
explanation: Wrong pair: the Eleventh Schedule deals with Panchayats; the powers of Municipalities are in the Twelfth. Fourth (Rajya Sabha seats), Fifth (Scheduled Areas) and Eighth (languages) are correct. (No printed key.)

notes.text: - **Wrong pairs asked:** "Ninth – allocation of seats in the Council of States" (that is the **Fourth**); "Eleventh – Municipalities" (that is the **Twelfth**; the Eleventh = Panchayats).

q: The State List contains:
explanation:
the State List had 66 subjects originally — now 61 (Union 100, Concurrent 52) after transfers such as the 42nd Amendment (NextGen Polity p.157)
The State List originally had 66 subjects (now 61); 97 was the original Union List. (Now 61 after transfers, mainly by the 42nd Amendment.)

exam: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Screening Test 2017
q: Which part of the Constitution helps in identifying PESA districts in Andhra Pradesh?
explanation: Scheduled Areas – where PESA 1996 applies – are declared under the Fifth Schedule; the Sixth covers tribal areas of Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram.

notes.text: - **PESA districts / Scheduled Areas** are identified under the **Fifth Schedule** (PESA 1996 extends Part IX to Fifth Schedule areas); the Sixth covers the four north-eastern States.

q: Which of the following is not mentioned in second schedule of the Constitution of India
options: Allocation of seats in the Council of states
Judges of Supreme Court and High Court
key_text: Allocation of seats in the Council of states
explanation: The Second Schedule covers emoluments of the President, Governors, Speaker/Deputy Speaker, Chairman/Deputy Chairman, judges of the SC and HCs and the CAG; allocation of Rajya Sabha seats is in the Fourth Schedule.

q: Which one of the following articles is NOT covered under the third schedule of the Indian Constitution?
explanation: Art. 213 is the Governor's ordinance power, not an oath. The Third Schedule covers oaths under Arts. 75(4) (Union Ministers), 99 (MPs), 124(6), 148(2), 164(3) and 188 (MLAs) and 219.

notes.text: - **Outside the Third Schedule:** President – **Art. 60**; Vice-President – **Art. 69**; Governor – **Art. 159**.

q: First Amendment to Indian Constitution added
explanation: The First Amendment Act, 1951 added the Ninth Schedule (with Art. 31B); the 10th, 11th and 12th came in 1985 and 1992.

notes.text: - Added by the **First Amendment Act, 1951** – the **first Schedule added** – during the prime ministership of **Jawaharlal Nehru** (not the 8th, 9th or 42nd Amendment).

q: As the reservation Quota exceeded to 69% the Tamil Nadu Law was placed beyond judicial review in Schedule
explanation: The Tamil Nadu 69% reservation law was placed in the Ninth Schedule (Art. 31B) by the 76th Amendment, 1994, beyond judicial review. The Tenth to Twelfth deal with other subjects.

notes.text: - The **Tamil Nadu Reservation Act, 1993/94** (69% reservation for SCs, STs and OBCs – above the 50% Indra Sawhney limit) was placed in the **IX Schedule** by the **76th Amendment Act, 1994** to shield it from judicial review.

q: First Constitution Amendment added ____ schedule to Indian constitution.
explanation: The First Amendment (1951) added the Ninth Schedule.

notes.text: - Added by the **First Amendment Act, 1951** – the **first Schedule added** – during the prime ministership of **Jawaharlal Nehru** (not the 8th, 9th or 42nd Amendment).
